rounds.fact: Answers.com built its early traffic by aggregating dictionary, encyclopedia, and reference content into a single searchable site, well before crowdsourced Q&A sites took over that space.
Funny or Die launched in 2007 co-founded by Will Ferrell, and its debut video 'The Landlord' became one of the most-watched comedy videos of the early web-video era.
Photobucket became the default way millions of MySpace users hosted images for their profiles, since MySpace itself didn't offer easy photo uploading in its early years.
Dogpile was a 'metasearch' engine that combined results from multiple search engines at once, a workaround from an era when no single search engine indexed the whole web well.
RealPlayer's streaming format was, for years, the primary way people watched video and listened to audio online, long before YouTube or Spotify existed.
